title: Gradient-aware KV cache quantization + continuous-batching interaction simulation and ops plan
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Investigate a gradient-aware quantization scheme for KV cache entries and measure how continuous batching strategies interact with per-entry compression. The goal is to reduce GPU memory footprint without violating latency SLOs or creating cohort-specific quality regressions. This ticket covers simulation, small-scale canary runs, and an ops playbook for rollout/fallback.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible simulation harness that models continuous batching behavior and per-request KV writes/reads
Quantization policies (FP8/INT8/INT4) instrumented with a gradient-importance proxy and tested across 3 models: 7B, 13B, 70B
Benchmarks showing memory reduction, median/p99 latency change, and end-to-end quality (perplexity and task-specific eval) vs baseline FP16 KV
A rollback strategy + runtime circuit breaker that triggers auto-fallback to higher-fidelity cache when quality regressions exceed threshold
Runbook and a small canary PR with telemetry dashboards and threshold alerts configured
experiment_plan: Build a lightweight simulation that replays traces from production (sampled convo prefixes, token distributions, batch coalescing patterns)
Implement gradient-importance score: offline proxy using token attention norms and token recency; score normalized per-request
Define three policy tiers: tier-A (FP8 with adaptive scale), tier-B (INT8 with per-entry scale table), tier-C (block INT4 for long-lived low-importance entries)
Run parameter sweep across per-entry decay windows, block sizes, and batching window durations (1ms, 5ms, 20ms) to capture continuous batching effects

Instrument end-to-end pipeline for: memory usage, kernel occupancy, average batch size, latency p50/p95/p99, cache miss/hit under quantized decode, and quality metrics (perplexity, ROUGE/F1 on a prompt set)
Small canary on Dedicated pool with 10% traffic (non-critical tenants) followed by 1% hosted API test if stable
dataset_and_models: Production sample traces anonymized (2025-01 to 2025-02) stored in gs://redwood-traces/kv-quant-sim
Prompt set for quality eval: mix of summarization, code-completion, and knowledge-recall (approx 4k prompts)
Models: open-architecture Llama-2-13B, community-70B-optimized, internal-repro-7B (represent typical cache sizes and kv lifetime distributions)
metrics: Memory delta (GB) per replica / percent reduction vs FP16 baseline
Latency p50/p95/p99 impact at target throughput (tokens/sec) with continuous batching engaged
Quality delta: perplexity change and task F1/ROUGE deltas per cohort
Cache fidelity events: fraction of requests that triggered fallback due to quantization-induced divergence
Kernel utilization and GPU OOM rate (simulated and canary)
initial_findings: Simulation shows a nonlinear quality cliff when batching windows increase beyond 10ms with aggressive INT4 block packing—likely due to mismatched per-entry scales across coalesced KV writes
Gradient-importance proxy correlates with downstream token influence (Spearman rho ~0.62) on the 13B model, enough signal to prioritize entries for higher-fidelity storage
FP8 with adaptive per-entry scale had the best memory/quality trade-off in steady-state traces, but introduced ~3-4% p99 latency increase due to extra scale-decode ops in hot paths
INT8 achieved larger memory savings but required careful per-block scale tables to avoid catastrophic divergences on long-tailed tokens
INT4 block packing helps cold-entry compression but amplifies quality variance across infrequent cohorts (enterprise customers with long documents saw regressions)
risks: Cohort-specific regressions (e.g., customers with long-context workflows) could be masked in aggregate dashboards
Runtime overhead of per-entry scale lookups may push latency beyond SLOs for small-batch/low-latency paths
Edge-case interactions between KV eviction heuristics and block INT4 compaction could increase read amplification and GPU memory churn
Complexity of rollout: multi-dimensional policy matrix (model-size x batching-window x tenant-tier) increases operational load
decisions: Proceed with gradient-aware prioritization as primary mechanism (per-entry importance -> fidelity tier) rather than global static thresholds
Adopt FP8-adaptive as the default tier for hosted API with conservative INT8/INT4 enabled behind Dedicated feature flags and tenant opt-ins
Implement an on-device circuit breaker: if within a sliding window quality regressions exceed 0.5% of eval prompts, auto-fallback to FP16 for affected shard
Require a canary rundown and a 72-hour stability window before scaling to 30% traffic
